abstract: Systematic reviews and meta-analysis: Faculty abstracts – General category Conference Code: OP-302: Efficacy of methylphenidate in adult-onset ADHD: A systematic review and meta-analysis M. Mohanalakshmi, Mohammed Gani, K. Sathish Babu, Banupriya, Rahul, J. Premalatha Department of Pharmacology, Government Medical College, Karur, Tamil Nadu, India Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults is associated with persistent inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity, and impaired quality of life (QoL). This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating methylphenidate (MPH) in adults (≥18 years) diagnosed per DSM/ICD criteria. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov (updated July 2025). Eligible studies assessed MPH monotherapy or MPH combined with cognitive- behavioural therapy (CBT) for ≥4 weeks, reporting outcomes on ADHD symptoms, QoL, functional impairment, and safety. Standardized mean differences (SMD) were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity assessed via I² statistics. Six meta-analyses (n=1, 200 MPH; n=900 placebo) showed a pooled SMD of 0.90 (95% CI 0.65–1.15) for core symptoms with optimized dosing; non-continuous release formulations achieved SMD 0.58. Greatest improvements were observed for inattention (d=0.68), followed by hyperactivity (d=0.51) and impulsivity (d=0.46). QoL improvements were small-to-moderate (SMD 0.38). MPH+CBT yielded additional functional gains (SMD 0.30–0.45) in limited trials. Common adverse events included decreased appetite (20%), dry mouth (15%), palpitations (13%), and headache (10%); discontinuations were low (4.3%). Mechanistic evidence from animal models supports MPH’s long-term benefits via neuronal remodeling, dopamine transporter normalization, neuroglial changes, and Wnt pathway activation, without structural brain loss. Clinical Implications: Optimal non-continuous release MPH (57–72 mg/day) should be considered a first-line pharmacological option for adult ADHD, with adjunctive CBT for patients requiring additional functional improvement. Conference Code: OP-311: Revefenacin in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of safety and clinical efficacy Siddhartha Dutta1, Rima Shah1, Shubha Singhal1, Mamta Singh2, Sagar Dholariya3 1Department of Pharmacology, AIIMS, Rajkot, Gujarat, India, 2Department of Ophthalmology, AIIMS, Rajkot, Gujarat, India, 3Department of Biochemistry, AIIMS, Rajkot, Gujarat, India Background: Revefenacin is a novel long-acting muscarinic antagonist for maintenance therapy in COPD. This systematic review and metanalysis aimed to assess the safety and efficacy of revefenacin in COPD. Methods: The online databases like PubMed/Medline, Cochrane-library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched until 28th August 2025 for studies comparing Revefenacin to placebo or active treatments using keywords such as “Revefenacin” and ‘COPD’. All statistical analysis were conducted with R. Posit Software and Review Manager (RevMan 5.4) software. A network meta-analysis (NMA) was conducted with frequentist methods. Results: Of the 118 titles searched; after removing duplicates, 75 studies were evaluated for eligibility. Finally, 11 RCTs were finally included. Revefenacin was compared with placebo and active control (tiotropium). A subgroup analysis was conducted based on the treatment duration. In the safety analysis, there was no significant difference between TAE [OR=0.98 (0.75, 1.29), I2=25%, p=0.91], SAE [OR=0.99 (0.60, 1.64), I2=0%, p=0.97], NSAE [OR=1.29 (0.66, 2.51), I2=85%, p=0.45] as compared to placebo, or tiotropium [TAE: OR=0.65 (0.32, 1.30), I2=82%, p=0.22], [SAE: OR=0.82 (0.57, 1.18), I2=0%, p=0.28] and [NSAE: OR=0.70 (0.35, 1.40), I2=79%, p=0.32] respectively. In NMA comparing rank of treatments, tiotropium had highest SUCRA and P scores for TAE (75%, 0.74) and SAE (65%, 0.63) followed by placebo in TAE (54%, 0.54) and revefenacin 175 in SAE (59%, 0.58). A significant change was observed with majority of efficacy parameters like change in trough FEV1 (Revefenacin vs. Placebo) [MD=145.15 (133.36, 156.94), I2=96%, p< 0.00001], MRMU [MD=-0.30 (-0.59, -0.02), I2=99%, p=0.04] and proportion of SGRQ [OR=1.58 (1.19, 2.10), I2=0%, p=0.002]. In NMA comparing rank of treatment for FEV1, tiotropium (81%, 0.85) had highest SUCRA and P scores followed by revefenacin 175 (74%, 0.76). Conclusion: This study demonstrates that revefenacin has a fair safety profile as compared to placebo or tiotropium and is more effective than placebo in therapy of COPD. Conference Code: OP-114: Emerging trends in machine learning – Driven fall detection: A review of deep learning architectures, sensor fusion, and edge computing for real-time applications E. Manivannan, A. Velusamy, P. Dharani Department of Pharmacology, Vinayaka Mission’s Kirupananda Variyar Medical College & Hospital, Salem, Tamil Nadu, India Introduction: The occurrence of falls creates danger for people who are older adults & those with limited mobility because it produces serious medical outcomes with extended disabilities.Current advances in real time fall detection as well as prevention systems emerged through the combination of machine learning techniques with Internet of Things devices. Objectives: The purpose of this review is to assess recent development in ML- based fall detection systems that focuses on the impact of ML models on fall detection precision, the function of IoT devices in providing wide scale invisible supervision & Emerging patterns alongside future research prospects in this field. Methodology: The research analyzed articles spanning from 2018 to 2025 which originated from IEEE Xplore & PubMed together with ACM Digital Library & Google Scholar. Research studies adopted two categories of sensors for detection whereby wearable sensors relied on IMUs & accelerometers while environmental sensors consisted of smart flooring & radar based detection systems. Results: Sahni et al together with other Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) based models using Long short term Memory (BiLSTM) presented the best accuracy at 97.8%. Limitations: False positives & sensitivity issues Computational overhead & Real time Processing User compliance & Acceptability. Conclusion: The application of ML & IoT like deep learning models have become dominant in detecting falls through their implementation of CNNs, BiLSTM & Transformers resulting accuracy being reported over 97%.
